items.text:
सानन्दं सदनं सुतास्तु सधियः कांता प्रियालापिनी
इच्छापूर्तिधनं स्वयोषितिरतिः स्वाज्ञापराः सेवकाः
आतिथ्यं शिवपूजनं प्रतिदिनं मिष्टान्नपानं गृहे
साधोः सुड्गमुपासते च सततं धन्यो गृहस्थाश्रमः ॥ १ ॥
items.tr:
sānandaṃ sadanaṃ sutāstu sadhiyaḥ kāṃtā priyālāpinī
icchāpūrtidhanaṃ svayoṣitiratiḥ svājñāparāḥ sevakāḥ
ātithyaṃ śivapūjanaṃ pratidinaṃ miṣṭānnapānaṃ gṛhe
sādhoḥ suḍgamupāsate ca satataṃ dhanyo gṛhasthāśramaḥ || 1 ||
items.en: Blessed is family life when the home is happy, the sons are wise, the wife speaks sweetly, there is enough money for one's needs, love stays with one's own wife, servants obey, guests are welcomed, Shiva is worshipped daily, there is good food and drink at home, and good people are always near.

items.text:
आर्तेषु विप्रेषु दयान्वितश्चे-
च्छ्रध्देण या स्वल्पमुपैति दानम् ।
अनन्तपारं समुपैति दानम् ।
यद्दीयते तन्न लभेद् द्विजेभ्यः ॥ २ ॥
items.tr:
ārteṣu vipreṣu dayānvitaśce-
cchradhdeṇa yā svalpamupaiti dānam |
anantapāraṃ samupaiti dānam |
yaddīyate tanna labhed dvijebhyaḥ || 2 ||
items.en: One who, full of kindness, gives even a little with faith to learned men in distress receives it back without end; what is given to them is never lost.

items.text:
दाक्षिण्यं स्वजने दया परजने शाठ्यं सदा दुर्जने
प्रीतिःसाधुजने स्मयः खलजने विद्वज्जने चार्जवम् ।
शौर्यं शत्रुजने क्षमा गुरुजने नारीजने धूर्तता
इत्थं ये पुरुषा कलासु कुशलास्तेष्वे लोकस्थितिः ॥ ३ ॥
items.tr:
dākṣiṇyaṃ svajane dayā parajane śāṭhyaṃ sadā durjane
prītiḥsādhujane smayaḥ khalajane vidvajjane cārjavam |
śauryaṃ śatrujane kṣamā gurujane nārījane dhūrtatā
itthaṃ ye puruṣā kalāsu kuśalāsteṣve lokasthitiḥ || 3 ||
items.en: Courtesy to one's own people, kindness to strangers, cleverness with the wicked, love for the good, coolness toward the base, honesty with the learned, courage before enemies, patience with elders, and shrewdness with women: the world rests on people skilled in these ways.

items.text:
हस्तौ दानविवर्जितौ श्रुतिपुटौ सारस्वतद्रोहिणौ
नेत्रे साधुविलोकनेन रहिते पादौ न तीर्थं गतौ ॥
अन्यायार्जितवित्त पूर्णमुदरं गर्वेण तुड्गं शिरो ।
रे रे जंबुक मुञ्चमुञ्च सहसा नीचं सुनिन्द्यं वपुः ॥ ४ ॥
items.tr:
hastau dānavivarjitau śrutipuṭau sārasvatadrohiṇau
netre sādhuvilokanena rahite pādau na tīrthaṃ gatau ||
anyāyārjitavitta pūrṇamudaraṃ garveṇa tuḍgaṃ śiro |
re re jaṃbuka muñcamuñca sahasā nīcaṃ sunindyaṃ vapuḥ || 4 ||
items.en: Hands that never gave, ears that never listened to learning, eyes that never looked on good people, feet that never went to holy places, a belly filled with money earned wrongly, and a head held high in pride: hey jackal, drop this low and shameful body at once!

items.text:
येषां श्रीमद्यशोदा सुतपदकमले नास्ति भक्तिर्नराणां
येषामाभीरकन्याप्रियगुणकथने नानुरक्ता रसज्ञा ।
येषां श्रीकृष्णलीलाललितरसकथा सादरौनैव कर्णौ
धिक्तांधिक्तांधिगेतांकथ यति सततं कीर्तनस्थोमॄदंगः ॥ ५ ॥
items.tr:
yeṣāṃ śrīmadyaśodā sutapadakamale nāsti bhaktirnarāṇāṃ
yeṣāmābhīrakanyāpriyaguṇakathane nānuraktā rasajñā |
yeṣāṃ śrīkṛṣṇalīlālalitarasakathā sādaraunaiva karṇau
dhiktāṃdhiktāṃdhigetāṃkatha yati satataṃ kīrtanasthomṝdaṃgaḥ || 5 ||
items.en: Those who have no devotion to the lotus feet of Yashoda's son, whose tongues take no joy in praising the beloved of the cowherd girls, and whose ears do not eagerly hear the sweet stories of Krishna's play: the drum at the hymn singing keeps beating out 'shame on them, shame, shame'.

items.text:
पत्रं नैव यदा करीरविटपे दोषो वसन्तस्य किं
नोलूकोऽप्यवलोकते यदि दिवा सूर्यस्य किं दूषणं ।
वर्षा नैव पतन्ति चातकमुखे मेघस्य किं दूषणं ।
यत्पूर्व विधिना ललाटलिखितं तन्मार्जितुं कः क्षमः ॥ ६ ॥
items.tr:
patraṃ naiva yadā karīraviṭape doṣo vasantasya kiṃ
nolūko'pyavalokate yadi divā sūryasya kiṃ dūṣaṇaṃ |
varṣā naiva patanti cātakamukhe meghasya kiṃ dūṣaṇaṃ |
yatpūrva vidhinā lalāṭalikhitaṃ tanmārjituṃ kaḥ kṣamaḥ || 6 ||
items.en: If the karira bush has no leaves, is spring to blame? If the owl cannot see by day, is the sun to blame? If no rain falls into the chataka bird's beak, is the cloud to blame? Who can wipe away what fate wrote on one's forehead long ago?

items.text:
सत्सङ्गाद भवति हि साधुता खलानां ।
साधूनां न हि खलसंगतेः खलत्वम् ॥
आमोदं कुसुमभवं मृदेव धत्ते
मृदगन्धं नहि कुसुमानि धारयन्ति ॥ ७ ॥
items.tr:
satsaṅgāda bhavati hi sādhutā khalānāṃ |
sādhūnāṃ na hi khalasaṃgateḥ khalatvam ||
āmodaṃ kusumabhavaṃ mṛdeva dhatte
mṛdagandhaṃ nahi kusumāni dhārayanti || 7 ||
items.en: The wicked can become good in good company, but the good do not become wicked in bad company; the earth takes on the scent of flowers, but flowers do not take on the smell of earth.

items.text:
साधूनां दर्शनं पुण्यं तीर्थीभूता हि साधवः ।
कालेन फलते तीर्थं सद्यः साधुसमागमः ॥ ८ ॥
items.tr:
sādhūnāṃ darśanaṃ puṇyaṃ tīrthībhūtā hi sādhavaḥ |
kālena phalate tīrthaṃ sadyaḥ sādhusamāgamaḥ || 8 ||
items.en: Seeing good people is a blessing, for they are like living holy places; a pilgrimage bears fruit in time, but meeting good people bears fruit at once.

items.text:
विप्राऽस्मिन्नगरे महान् कथयकस्तालद्रुमाणां गणः
को दाता रजको ददाति वसनं प्रातर्गृ हीत्वा निशि ।
को दक्षः परवित्तदारहरणे सर्वोऽपि दक्षो जनः
कस्माज्जीवसि हे सखे विष कृमिन्यायेन जीवाम्यहम् ॥ ९ ॥
items.tr:
viprā'sminnagare mahān kathayakastāladrumāṇāṃ gaṇaḥ
ko dātā rajako dadāti vasanaṃ prātargṛ hītvā niśi |
ko dakṣaḥ paravittadāraharaṇe sarvo'pi dakṣo janaḥ
kasmājjīvasi he sakhe viṣa kṛminyāyena jīvāmyaham || 9 ||
items.en: 'Brahmin, who is great in this town?' 'The palm trees.' 'Who is generous?' 'The washerman, who takes clothes in the morning and gives them back at night.' 'Who is clever?' 'Everyone is clever at taking others' wealth and wives.' 'Then how do you live, friend?' 'I live like a worm in poison.'

items.text:
न विप्रपादोदकपंकजानि
न वेदशास्त्रध्वनिगर्जितानि ।
स्वाहास्वधाकारविवर्जितानि
श्मशानतुल्यानिगृहाणि तानि ॥ १० ॥
items.tr:
na viprapādodakapaṃkajāni
na vedaśāstradhvanigarjitāni |
svāhāsvadhākāravivarjitāni
śmaśānatulyānigṛhāṇi tāni || 10 ||
items.en: Homes where the feet of learned men are never washed, where the sound of the Vedas is never heard, and where no offerings are made to gods and ancestors are no better than cremation grounds.

items.text:
सत्यं माता पिता ज्ञानं धर्मो भ्राता दया सखा
शांतिः पत्नी क्षमा पुत्रः षडेते ममबान्धवाः ॥ ११ ॥
items.tr:
satyaṃ mātā pitā jñānaṃ dharmo bhrātā dayā sakhā
śāṃtiḥ patnī kṣamā putraḥ ṣaḍete mamabāndhavāḥ || 11 ||
items.en: Truth is my mother, knowledge my father, righteousness my brother, kindness my friend, peace my wife and forgiveness my son: these six are my family.

items.text:
अनित्यानि शरिराणि विभवो नैव शाश्वतः ।
नित्यं सन्निहितो मृत्युः कर्तव्यो धर्मसंग्रहः ॥ १२ ॥
items.tr:
anityāni śarirāṇi vibhavo naiva śāśvataḥ |
nityaṃ sannihito mṛtyuḥ kartavyo dharmasaṃgrahaḥ || 12 ||
items.en: Bodies do not last, wealth does not stay forever, and death is always near; so one should gather good deeds.

items.text:
निमन्त्रणोत्सवा विप्रा गावो नवतृणोत्सवाः ।
पत्युत्साहयुता भार्या अहं कृष्ण ! रणोत्सवः ॥ १३ ॥
items.tr:
nimantraṇotsavā viprā gāvo navatṛṇotsavāḥ |
patyutsāhayutā bhāryā ahaṃ kṛṣṇa ! raṇotsavaḥ || 13 ||
items.en: Brahmins delight in invitations to a feast, cows in fresh grass, and a wife in her husband's joy; but I, O Krishna, delight in battle.

items.text:
मातृवत्परदारेषु परद्रव्याणि लोष्ठवत् ।
आत्मवत्सर्वभूतानि यः पश्यति स पंडितः ॥ १४ ॥
items.tr:
mātṛvatparadāreṣu paradravyāṇi loṣṭhavat |
ātmavatsarvabhūtāni yaḥ paśyati sa paṃḍitaḥ || 14 ||
items.en: One who sees other men's wives as his mother, other people's wealth as a lump of clay, and all beings as himself is truly wise.

items.text:
धर्मे तत्परता मुखे मधुरता दाने समुत्साहता
मित्रेऽवंचकता गुरौ विनयता चित्तेऽतिगम्भीरता ।
आचारे शुचिता गुणे रसिकता शास्त्रेषु विज्ञातृता
रूपे सुन्दरता शिवे भजनता त्वय्यस्तिभी राघवः ॥ १५ ॥
items.tr:
dharme tatparatā mukhe madhuratā dāne samutsāhatā
mitre'vaṃcakatā gurau vinayatā citte'tigambhīratā |
ācāre śucitā guṇe rasikatā śāstreṣu vijñātṛtā
rūpe sundaratā śive bhajanatā tvayyastibhī rāghavaḥ || 15 ||
items.en: O Raghava, in you there is devotion to right living, sweetness in speech, eagerness to give, no deceit toward friends, humility before teachers, great depth of mind, purity in conduct, love of good qualities, knowledge of the scriptures, beauty of form, and devotion to Shiva.

items.text:
काष्ठं कल्पतरुः सुमेरुरचलश्चिन्तामणिः प्रस्तरः
सूर्यस्तीव्रकरः शशीक्षयकरः क्षारोहि वारां निधिः ।
कामो नष्टतनुर्बलिदितिसुतो नित्यं पशुः कामगाः
नैस्तांस्ते तुलयामि भो रघुपते कस्योपमादीयते ॥ १६ ॥
items.tr:
kāṣṭhaṃ kalpataruḥ sumeruracalaścintāmaṇiḥ prastaraḥ
sūryastīvrakaraḥ śaśīkṣayakaraḥ kṣārohi vārāṃ nidhiḥ |
kāmo naṣṭatanurbaliditisuto nityaṃ paśuḥ kāmagāḥ
naistāṃste tulayāmi bho raghupate kasyopamādīyate || 16 ||
items.en: The wish-granting tree is only wood, Mount Meru cannot move, the wish-granting gem is only stone, the sun's rays are harsh, the moon wanes, the ocean is salty, the god of love has no body, Bali was a demon, and the wish-granting cow is an animal. O Lord of the Raghus, I cannot compare you with these; with what, then, can you be compared?

items.text:
विद्या मित्रं प्रवासे च भार्या मित्र गृहे च ।
व्याधिस्तस्यौषधं मित्रं धर्मा मित्रं मृतस्य च ॥ १७ ॥
items.tr:
vidyā mitraṃ pravāse ca bhāryā mitra gṛhe ca |
vyādhistasyauṣadhaṃ mitraṃ dharmā mitraṃ mṛtasya ca || 17 ||
items.en: Learning is a friend when you travel, a wife is a friend at home, medicine is a friend to the sick, and good deeds are a friend after death.

items.text:
विनयं राजपुत्रेभ्यः पंडितेभ्यः सुभाषितम् ।
अनृतं द्यूतकारेभ्यः स्त्रीभ्यः शिक्षेत कैतवम् ॥ १८ ॥
items.tr:
vinayaṃ rājaputrebhyaḥ paṃḍitebhyaḥ subhāṣitam |
anṛtaṃ dyūtakārebhyaḥ strībhyaḥ śikṣeta kaitavam || 18 ||
items.en: Learn good manners from princes, fine speech from the learned, lying from gamblers, and trickery from women.

items.text:
अनालोक्य व्ययं कर्ता अनाथः कलहप्रियः ।
आर्तः स्त्रीसर्वक्षेत्रेषु नरः शीघ्र विनश्यति ॥ १९ ॥
items.tr:
anālokya vyayaṃ kartā anāthaḥ kalahapriyaḥ |
ārtaḥ strīsarvakṣetreṣu naraḥ śīghra vinaśyati || 19 ||
items.en: A man who spends without thinking, has no one to support him, loves to quarrel, and chases women everywhere is soon ruined.

items.text:
नाऽऽहारं चिन्तयेत्प्राज्ञो धर्ममेकं हि चिन्तयेत् ।
आहारो हि मनुष्याणां जन्मना सह जायते ॥ २० ॥
items.tr:
nā''hāraṃ cintayetprājño dharmamekaṃ hi cintayet |
āhāro hi manuṣyāṇāṃ janmanā saha jāyate || 20 ||
items.en: A wise person should not worry about food; he should think only about right living, for a person's food is decided at the time of his birth.

items.text:
धनधान्यप्रयोगेषु विद्यासंग्रहणे तथा ।
आहारे व्यवहारे च त्यक्तलज्जः सुखीभवेत् ॥ २१ ॥
items.tr:
dhanadhānyaprayogeṣu vidyāsaṃgrahaṇe tathā |
āhāre vyavahāre ca tyaktalajjaḥ sukhībhavet || 21 ||
items.en: One who sets shyness aside in dealing with money and grain, in gaining knowledge, in eating, and in business will be happy.

items.text:
जलबिन्दुनिपातेन क्रमशः पूर्यते घटः ।
स हेतु सर्वविद्यानां धर्मस्य च धनस्य च ॥ २२ ॥
items.tr:
jalabindunipātena kramaśaḥ pūryate ghaṭaḥ |
sa hetu sarvavidyānāṃ dharmasya ca dhanasya ca || 22 ||
items.en: A pot is filled little by little, one drop of water at a time; that is also the way to gain all learning, good deeds and wealth.

items.text:
वयसः परिणामेऽपि यः खलः खलः एव सः ।
सम्पक्वमपि माधुर्यं नापयातीन्द्रवारुणम् ॥ २३ ॥
items.tr:
vayasaḥ pariṇāme'pi yaḥ khalaḥ khalaḥ eva saḥ |
sampakvamapi mādhuryaṃ nāpayātīndravāruṇam || 23 ||
items.en: A wicked person stays wicked even in old age; the bitter gourd does not lose its bitterness even when it is fully ripe.
